Engineering, Ph.D.
Build an Engineering, Ph.D. That Works
On Campus

48-81
Credit Hours
4-6 Years
Avg Completion
Your goals should shape your engineering doctoral program. At Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, you’ll be able to design an individualized course of study that focuses your research interests, strengthens your technical expertise, and prepares you for the work you want to do.
Program Details
The Ph.D. in Engineering equips engineers with the skills needed for advanced careers in industry, government, and academia through specialized study and original research.
Choose from four engineering concentrations:
Civil and Environmental Engineering
Electrical and Advanced Manufacturing
Industrial and Process Engineering
Mechanical and Energy Engineering
Throughout the program, you'll strengthen your technical foundation, explore artificial intelligence and machine learning as tools for solving complex problems, conduct original research, and develop the specialized expertise you'll need to advance your career.
What You’ll Learn
Coursework emphasizes:
Advanced engineering analysis to evaluate and solve complex technical problems.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning for engineering applications.
Computational modeling and simulation to analyze, test, and optimize engineering systems.
Data analysis and engineering analytics to support technical decision-making.
Specialized study in civil and environmental, electrical and advanced manufacturing, industrial and process, or mechanical and energy engineering.
Research methods that prepare you to plan, conduct, and communicate original engineering research.
Technical communication through scholarly writing, presentations, and dissertation research.

Career Outcomes
Graduates of the Ph.D. in Engineering are prepared for advanced technical, research, and leadership roles, including:
Research and Development Engineer
Research Program Manager
Government Research Scientist / Engineer
National Laboratory Researcher
Senior Systems Engineer
Chief Engineer
Engineering Manager / Director
Technical Program Manager
Technical Fellow
Engineering Consultant
Director of Research and Development
University Faculty Member
Salary & Job Outlook
Engineering professionals with advanced degrees often qualify for senior technical, research, and leadership positions with competitive earning potential. Depending on specialization, industry, and experience, typical salaries range from approximately $100,000 to more than $170,000 annually, with many engineering management and research leadership roles exceeding that range. Employment opportunities remain strong as demand grows for engineers in advanced manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, computing, artificial intelligence, and research and development.
Salary ranges are based on data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook Handbook and national compensation aggregators such as PayScale and Salary.com, reflecting typical earnings for credentialed professionals in the field.
The TAMU-CC Advantage
At Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, your doctoral studies begin with your goals. You’ll work closely with experienced faculty who will help you choose the coursework, research direction, professional experiences, and connections that support the career you want. Faculty will guide your research and publication plans, connect you with additional mentors, and help you pursue internships and other professional opportunities.
You’ll learn from leading researchers working across diverse areas, including autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, water resources, advanced manufacturing, energy and infrastructure. Their projects are supported by agencies including the National Science Foundation, Department of Defense, Department of Energy, Department of Transportation and NASA.
The program also connects doctoral students with industry partners and government laboratories through internships, collaborative projects, and faculty networks. Grant-supported research assistantships and summer internships may provide funding as you gain experience beyond the classroom.
At TAMU-CC, you’ll find:
An individualized doctoral program aligned with your background, interests, and professional goals
Close guidance from experienced faculty throughout your studies
Faculty expertise across four engineering concentrations and emerging technologies
Connections with industry, government laboratories, research organizations, and funding agencies
Internship, research assistantship, and professional networking opportunities
Support for research, publication, funding proposals, and career development
An interdisciplinary environment where you can draw from engineering, computer science, mathematics, and related fields
Want to learn more? Fill out our contact form and a graduate admissions counselor will connect with you soon, or connect directly with the program coordinator.
How to Apply
Applying is much easier when you're supported—and at TAMU-CC, our graduate admissions counselors are here to help.
To get started, you’ll need a master's degree in engineering or a closely related field. Exceptional applicants with a bachelor's degree in engineering may also be considered for direct admission to the Ph.D. program.
To apply, you will need to submit:
A completed application for admission
Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
A statement of purpose describing your research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing the Ph.D.
A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV)
Three letters of recommendation
International Students also submit:
English proficiency scores and Visa documentation
Application Deadlines
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as they are received. To receive full consideration, apply by the priority deadline.

We’re Here to Help
Sometimes getting started is the hardest part. If you have any questions or need help with your application, we've got you covered. Just fill out the information request form or contact our program coordinator directly for assistance.
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need a master's degree to apply?
Not necessarily. Applicants with a master's degree in engineering or a closely related field are encouraged to apply. Exceptional students with a bachelor's degree in engineering may also be considered for direct admission to the Ph.D. program.
Can I customize my degree plan?
Yes. You'll work with faculty to develop a program of study that aligns with your research interests, technical strengths, and professional goals while meeting all degree requirements.
What engineering concentrations are available?
Students may pursue one of four concentrations:
Civil and Environmental Engineering
Electrical and Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
Industrial and Process Engineering
Mechanical and Energy Engineering
Will I have opportunities to conduct research?
Yes. Original research is a central part of the doctoral experience. Students complete a dissertation while working with faculty conducting research across a variety of engineering disciplines and emerging technologies.
Are internships required?
Internships are encouraged but not required. The program emphasizes opportunities to gain research experience through industry partnerships, government laboratories, and externally funded research projects.
Is financial assistance available?
Graduate teaching assistantships and research assistantships may be available, depending on available institutional and external grant funding.
What makes this program different?
Rather than following a one-size-fits-all curriculum, you'll work closely with faculty to develop a doctoral experience that supports your research interests and career goals. Along the way, you'll have opportunities to collaborate with researchers, build professional connections, pursue internships, and gain experience through funded research projects.
